          <p class="separator" data-blogger-escaped-style="clear: both; text-align: left;">A TTL-USB converter is essentially required for the direct interfacing of modules to the PC, without an intermediate microcontroller or similar platform.</p>
<div>
<p>For different applications of modules like GSM, GPS.., etc., a TTL-USB or RS232-USB converters (mostly TTL-USB  converter) is the best option to interface with PC or USB port.</p>
<p>If we have an Arduino UNO, Arduino Mega,.. Or similar boards, we can simply use that board for serial communication between PC & module, without a TTL-USB converter. The serial communication on Arduino boards is through the USB interface with its inbuilt ATMEGA8U2 chip. ATMEGA8U2 chip act as a USB serial bridge between the computer’s USB port and the main processor’s serial port.</p>
<p>To use an Arduino board as a TTL-USB converter.</p>
<p class="">Reset the board by grounding the reset pin; just connect a wire from reset pin to ground.<img fetchpriority="high" decoding="async" class="aligncenter wp-image-2511 tc-smart-loaded" src="https://mechatrofice.com/wp-content/uploads/2017/03/USB-to-TTL-converter-using-arduino-UNO-R3-300x284.jpg" alt="arduino usb to ttl converter" width="362" height="343" sizes="(max-width: 362px) 100vw, 362px" srcset="https://mechatrofice.com/wp-content/uploads/2017/03/USB-to-TTL-converter-using-arduino-UNO-R3-300x284.jpg 300w, https://mechatrofice.com/wp-content/uploads/2017/03/USB-to-TTL-converter-using-arduino-UNO-R3.jpg 400w"></p>
</div>
<h2 class="fittexted_for_content_h2" style="font-size: 38.25px;">Arduino to serial connection</h2>
<table style="height: 116px;" width="377">
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="width: 180px;">Arduino UNO pins</td>
<td style="width: 181px;">Module Pin</td>
</tr>
<tr class="alt">
<td style="width: 180px;">Digital pin 0 (RX)</td>
<td style="width: 181px;">RX</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="width: 180px;">Digital pin 1 (TX)</td>
<td style="width: 181px;">TX</td>
</tr>
<tr class="alt">
<td style="width: 180px;">GND</td>
<td style="width: 181px;">GND</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<p>Connect the RX pin on the Arduino board to the RX, TX to TX and GND to GND of the module.</p>
<p>Connect the board to a USB port; through a USB type A  type B cable. Open serial monitor or hyper terminal or any serial communication terminal. And select the serial port of the board, e.g: – com1, com2, com3,…, etc..</p>
<p>Now the serial communication will perform directly between the computer and the module.</p>
